intro.heading: Rooted in community.
body: Heartfelt gatherings in the desert. That's the work. Somebody cooks, everybody sits down, and a few hours later nobody wants to leave.
We're a woman-owned catering company in Joshua Tree. Local ingredients, cooked by hand, never locked into a single cuisine.
Connection through food is the whole point. The menu is just how we get there.

image.alt: Squash blossom pizza with pesto and parmesan on a wooden peel over patterned tile

services.heading: What we offer
services.intro: Every one of these starts the same way: somebody's table, the people around it, and food we cook by hand for them. Dinner for eight or a hundred in a backyard, the care is the same. Real ingredients, a menu written for your people, and a kitchen that loves doing this.

items.name: Event Catering
items.description: Weddings, birthdays, anniversaries, the big backyard nights. We serve and clean up after, so you can be a guest at your own party. Menus are built around your guest list, not pulled off a shelf.

image.alt: Two candlelit tables set for dinner among the boulders at dusk, a Joshua tree beside them

items.name: Retreat Meals
items.description: Multi-day cooking for groups staying out in the desert. Breakfast before everyone scatters, packed lunches for the day, dinner when they come back hungry. We plan the whole arc so nobody's thinking about food.

image.alt: Friends reaching across a long table for a fennel and apple salad, roasted chicken and potatoes

items.name: Private Chef
items.description: We cook in your kitchen, your house, your rental, wherever you're staying. Courses come out when they're ready, and you get to sit down for all of them.

image.alt: Sliced steak with roasted fennel and a chopped pepper salsa on a white plate

items.name: Production Catering
items.description: Cast and crew meals for shoots working out here. We'll feed everyone properly and keep it moving. Dietary needs handled without a fuss.

image.alt: Crew breakfast platters: fruit, smoked salmon with cucumber, red onion, tomato and dill, and a tub of dill cream cheese with the JTCC sticker

items.name: Meal Prepping
items.description: Cooked, portioned, and delivered with reheating instructions. Right for a house full of people over a long weekend, or a week you'd rather not spend cooking.

image.alt: A tray of slow-roasted pulled pork with orange slices and chopped herbs

services.pricingNote: Every menu is written for the event, so every quote is too. Tell us the date, the headcount, and what you're picturing.
services.aside: Same kitchen, same hands, same care either way. Every menu is written for the table it's headed to.

testimonials.intro: Real reviews from real nights. More on Google.

quotes.quote: We recently had a most excellent private dining experience and chef Kristi thought over everything to make it special.

I contacted a handful of caterers in the area while planning our trip, but really loved their flexibility and offerings. Kristi and Cat made this bachelorette weekend so special with personalized menus and touches.
The menu options were terrific with a lot of special touches that made it bespoke for the event. Working with them makes me want to throw more parties!
They brought so many creative and personal touch ideas from the start and took care of so many details. We also had some dietary restrictions and they went above and beyond to accommodate.
JTCC provided catering for our production in Twentynine Palms. Kristi worked with our budget and the cast and crew were so happy with her delicious menu and beautiful presentation.
They catered our small wedding ceremony and the food was amazing and they were very timely and responsive. It was the perfect buffet-style taco bar for our guests!

about.heading: About
about.lede: Joshua Tree Catering Co. is a woman-owned catering company in the high desert, founded and run by Chef Kristi.
body: Kristi has spent more than 20 years working in restaurants, in just about every position you can imagine. She knows what it takes to make an event feel effortless, and how much work goes on behind the scenes to make sure the people at the party never have to think about any of it.

But it really started in her grandmother’s bakery. Kristi grew up in Southern California in a family of cooks and bakers, and the bakery was where she first learned her way around a kitchen and watched a small food business become part of the fabric of a neighborhood.

Her dad taught her the rest. Growing up in a Romanian family, the year had a rhythm to it: sarmale at the holidays, mămăligă on the stove, cozonac coming out of the oven in December. Every gathering somehow ended up in the kitchen, and that’s really where her love of feeding people comes from.

She started cooking in Joshua Tree much the same way, with dinner parties, friends’ birthdays, whatever someone happened to be celebrating. Word travels quickly in a small town, and somewhere along the way, those dinners turned into Joshua Tree Catering Co.

We cook everything by hand, sourcing locally whenever we can and working with local growers and makers whenever it makes sense. We’ve also never been interested in being tied to one kind of food. It might be tacos one weekend and a Spanish dinner the next. Every event is different, and that’s part of what we love about it.

At the end of the day, food is a universal language. Someone cooks, everyone sits down, and a few hours later nobody wants to leave. Getting to be a small part of those moments, and of this community’s table, is something we don’t take for granted.
